mechanism_narrative: The recent stabilization of WORKPLACES mobility at a significantly depressed level, following a period of recovery, indicates a new baseline for office attendance that will continue to suppress general weekday footfall, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days in more than 50% of instances where WORKPLACES remained stable or declined.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below 5% from baseline, it signifies a critical mass of people spending less time at home and more time out, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as they seek out-of-home activities.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days when RESIDENTIAL falls below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent low levels of TRANSIT combined with the stabilization of WORKPLACES mobility suggest that while some people are returning to work, they are avoiding public transport, limiting spontaneous retail trips and thus suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite TRANSIT remaining below -35% and WORKPLACES below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of continued social distancing, the recent sharp decline in PARKS mobility indicates reduced outdoor leisure activity, which will divert some discretionary spending towards indoor retail, leading to a slight increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days, even if PARKS mobility remains below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: The stable, slightly positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates consistent essential activity, but its lack of significant growth suggests no broader surge in general out-of-home activity, thus RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining within 0% to 5% of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dip in RETAIL_REC below -13% for two consecutive weeks signals a loss of consumer confidence or increased caution, which will lead to a further decline in retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls below -13% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days after falling below -13% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its slight downward trend while PARKS mobility remains significantly depressed, it suggests people are shifting from home-based leisure to other out-of-home activities, potentially boosting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0% AND PARKS remains below -25%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days when RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0% and PARKS remains below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained low level of TRANSIT mobility, indicative of ongoing public health advisories against non-essential travel or reduced public transport capacity, will continue to constrain access to central retail areas, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite TRANSIT remaining below -35%.
